canonical.title: Malaysia, Coast to Coast to Borneo: A First-Timer's 2–3 Week Crossing

siblings.title: Why visit Malaysia: the case for your first Southeast-Asia trip
siblings.summary: Five reasons Malaysia is the most rewarding first step into Southeast Asia — best street food on the continent, wild orangutans, the planet's oldest rainforest, living UNESCO cities — all in fluent English, visa-free, on a euro that goes far.

siblings.title: Getting to Malaysia from Ghent + entry/visa for a Belgian couple (2026)
siblings.summary: Fly into KLIA (Kuala Lumpur) — it's the cheapest, best-connected, and natural start of a West-Coast route; Belgians get 90 days visa-free but must file the free MDAC within 3 days of arrival.

siblings.title: Getting between the bases: internal transport for a routed Malaysia trip (2026)
siblings.summary: Fly the long and awkward hops, take the train/bus for the short scenic west-coast ones; every Borneo hop and the cross-peninsula jump to the Perhentians is a flight.

siblings.title: When to Visit Malaysia: One Trip, Three Regions, One Window
siblings.summary: Late March–May is the one window where the east-coast islands and Borneo are both open and dry while the haze hasn't yet arrived; June–July is the runner-up.

siblings.title: Malaysia First-Visit Prep: Money, SIM, Health, Etiquette, Safety & Budget
siblings.summary: Practical money, SIM, health, etiquette, safety and per-couple budget prep for a Belgian couple's first 2-3 week Malaysia trip in 2026.

siblings.title: Malaysia in 2-3 weeks: the routed first-visit itinerary
siblings.summary: One sensible order for a first Malaysia trip: a west-coast sweep, an east-coast wild leg, then Borneo - with a recommended nights-split, 12-14 day and 3-week+ variants, and the Nov-Feb monsoon reroute.
